summary: All three original bridge findings are resolved within the documented supported API and header-container contract. Independently inspected fixes and reran full offline Hermes suite and actual corrected-main C integration in normal and sanitizer configurations. Narrow bridge approval only; not M3 acceptance.

findings_resolution.verification: Actual C integration on both corrected main binaries: A public-frontier pin accepted (200), honest A private destination rejected (403), complete valid B headers through A rejected (403), same attack against compatible baseline also rejected (403). Canonical A task/session/branch/generation retained, invalid lowercase generation fence appended, no invocation fabricated; only initial request reaches scripted upstream.

Full suite exercises same-case and case-variant duplicates, conflicting and identical values, list pairs, single-use iterators, stdlib Message, and multi_items() with lossy items(). Every duplicate is fenced before conversion; separate iterator test verifies unrelated Keep header survives and a valid invocation is issued. Actual C tests reject list-pair duplicates and last-value-wins case-folded fences with 403 on normal and sanitizer builds.

Test injects RuntimeError and KeyboardInterrupt at each of four registration steps. All returned handles disposed in reverse order, unrelated callback preserved, owned exporter worker dead before install re-raises. Source inspection confirms dispose() is a supported public PluginRegistration API in local hermes_cli/plugins.py (1231 onward), with register_hook returning such a handle (3387-3410). Tests use minimal public-contract fixtures, not a full native Hermes runtime.

tests.sanitizer_verification: Integration launcher requires clean process exit and checks stderr for AddressSanitizer and runtime error diagnostics; both tests passed.
